behavioral_effects: The backend relation layer is extracted: 108 fully qualified API routes with module attribution, 5 Taskiq tasks, 15 ORM models with table names, 98 test-to-module TESTS edges, and the 6-product 88-tool Google registry - all with zero unknowns on the real tree.
compatibility_impact: None. New extractor with no callers outside its tests; no generated output changed and sync moved zero bytes.
follow_up: Session 6.4 stores the three extraction layers in the SQLite cache and adds cycle and orphan analysis over them.
limitations: ROUTES_TO by direct import yields only 5 edges because routes reach services through app.api.deps dependency injection; the transitive route-to-service chain already exists in the import graph, so impact analysis is not blinded by this.
reason: The graph knows modules and imports but not what the modules are: impact cannot tell a route module from a task module, the site join in 7.1 has no api-route nodes to land on, and Google tools are registry rows no import edge will ever reveal; this extracts the relation layer the vocabulary already declares
risks: Route prefixes are resolved through the v1 registry only; a router included elsewhere keeps a router-relative path and is recorded as an unknown rather than misnamed.
rollback: git revert of the single commit; nothing consumes the extractor yet.
security_impact: None. Read-only AST extraction; the Google registry is read as a table of tool names and descriptions, never values or credentials, and per-user MCP tools remain runtime-evidence only per the vocabulary.
summary: Extract route, task, model, test, and tool relations

validators_run.evidence_ref: 258 passed in 112s, includes 14 new relation tests
